desc:
An AI document review and summary workflow reads the contracts, invoices, forms and reports you receive, then returns a short summary and a list of items for a person to check. Ecom Swift LLC builds it around your document types and your own flag rules.

## What is an AI document review workflow?

An AI document review workflow is an automated first read of incoming files. A document arrives in a shared folder or inbox, the workflow extracts the key facts, writes a brief summary and checks the file against rules you set. A person then reviews the summary and any flagged items instead of reading every page from the top.

It does not replace the reviewer. It prepares the file so the reviewer starts with the important parts already found.

## Why manual review slows teams down

Documents pile up in inboxes. A supplier contract needs its renewal date found, an application needs its missing fields spotted, an invoice needs its total compared with an order. Each task is simple, but doing it across dozens of files a week is slow, and tired readers miss details.

Late discovery is the costly part. A renewal date noticed after it passes, or an odd clause noticed after signing, creates problems that a quick first read would have caught.

## How the workflow improves results

The main gain is time. Reviewers spend their attention on exceptions rather than on routine reading. Key dates and amounts land in a sheet, so they can be sorted, searched and tracked, rather than buried in attachments.

Consistency improves too. The same checklist is applied to every file in the same way, regardless of who is on shift. Page references on each summary let the reviewer confirm any claim in seconds, which keeps trust in the output grounded in the source document.

## What a good document review setup includes

- A defined list of the document types it handles.
- A short summary written in plain language for each file.
- Extracted fields such as parties, dates, amounts, reference numbers and deadlines.
- A page reference beside each summary point.
- Flag rules you choose, for example a missing signature or an unusual payment term.
- A results sheet that stores every summary and field.
- Alerts when a flag is raised.
- A comparison against your own checklist where useful.
- A reviewer approval step before anything is acted on.

## What we do

We collect examples of each document type and agree on the fields and flag rules with you. Then we build the intake, whether that is a watched folder or a dedicated inbox, and connect the reading step to your results sheet. We test it on real past documents and adjust until the summaries and flags match what your reviewers would pick.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of document types, fields, flag rules and testing. At the top level we add a comparison against your checklist, an approval step and a handover guide.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide your flag rules before the build starts.
- Provide clean examples of each document type.
- Keep a person responsible for every final decision.
- Check page references when a summary looks surprising.
- Store files only in places your team already controls.

**Avoid:**
- Treating a summary as legal or financial advice.
- Sending documents you are not permitted to share.
- Mixing unrelated document types in one setup.
- Acting on a flagged item without reading the source page.
- Expecting perfect results from blurry scans or unreadable handwriting.

## Who it is for

A small property or trade business that receives supplier contracts and needs renewal dates tracked can use it. A finance assistant who checks invoices against orders all day can use it for a faster first pass. A team that handles applications or onboarding forms can use it to spot missing information before a file goes further.

## What we need from you

Send a handful of sample documents with private details removed, a short list of the facts you want pulled out and the situations that should raise a flag. Tell us where files arrive today. We never need passwords. Access to your folder, inbox or sheet is given through a limited collaborator or team account, and your private files stay in tools you already control.
